about: Where the ten reference checks in plain-words.json differ from docs/v2-ui-simple.md, "Ten checks, written out", so the document can be edited to match. `field` is the JSON's (plainWhat[n] and plainFix[n] count from 0), `documentLine` the document's label. `old` is the document's text, null where the document has none; `new` is the text to put there. A check with an empty list is still the document's, word for word. Built by reference_changes.py from the two files, not typed.

robots-txt-unreachable.new: A rules file that search engines can't read
robots-txt-unreachable.why: New optional field. The title is a sentence about the site, which reads as a finding beside "Not checked" in the "couldn't be checked" list; this noun phrase is shown there in its place.

internal-client-error.old: Every page and file on the site can be found
internal-client-error.new: No page or file answers with a "not found" error
internal-client-error.why: Review, accepted. Beside a failing "Pages or files that don't answer" or "Pages or files that fail with a server error", the old line reads as untrue. The new one says only what this check tested.

broken-internal-links.old: Every link on the site leads to a working page
broken-internal-links.new: Every link between your pages leads to a working page
broken-internal-links.why: Review, accepted. The check covers links between the site's own pages only, so the old line sat, untrue, beside a failing "Links to other websites that don't work".

empty-anchor-text.old: Every link has words to read
empty-anchor-text.new: Every link between your pages has words to read
empty-anchor-text.why: Review, accepted. The rule tests only links to the site's own addresses, so a site whose links to other websites have no words passes, and "Every link has words to read" was then untrue.

empty-anchor-text.new: Pages are still found either way, so it can wait.
empty-anchor-text.why: Asked for with the review: a Notice says when it is fine, and this one didn't. No honest "then there is nothing to do" exists for a link with no words (it is always a fault for screen-reader users), so the sentence says it can wait, as the five other Notices of that kind do. 69 words in all, inside the 70.

duplicate-site-version.new: A site that answers at more than one address
duplicate-site-version.why: New optional field. The title is a sentence about the site, which reads as a finding beside "Not checked" in the "couldn't be checked" list; this noun phrase is shown there in its place.

image-too-large.old: Some pages show images whose files are over 200 KB.
image-too-large.new: Some pages show images whose files are over {limit:largeImageBytes}.
image-too-large.readsWithTheDefault: Some pages show images whose files are over 200 KB.
image-too-large.why: 200 KB is the default of the analysis setting largeImageBytes, which Advanced can change: the sentence was untrue once it is. The engine fills the token with the number and its unit, so with the default it reads exactly as the document's sentence does.

title-duplicate.old: Every page has its own title
title-duplicate.new: No two pages share a title
title-duplicate.why: Review, accepted. The old line is printed as good news on a site whose pages have no title at all (title-missing fails, this check passes). The other duplicates have the same form: "No two pages share a search description".

slow-response.old: These pages took more than 1 second to arrive when the check asked for them.
slow-response.new: These pages took more than {limit:slowResponseMs} to arrive when the check asked for them.
slow-response.readsWithTheDefault: These pages took more than 1 second to arrive when the check asked for them.
slow-response.why: 1 second is the default of the analysis setting slowResponseMs, which Advanced can change: the sentence was untrue once it is. The engine fills the token with the number and its unit, so with the default it reads exactly as the document's sentence does.

alsoInTheDocument.change: A row for `plainLooksFor`: optional; a noun phrase for what the check looks for, shown in the "couldn't be checked" list where the title is a sentence; 60 characters, no full stop. 12 checks have one.

alsoInTheDocument.where: The rules, "Numbers carry their unit and their limit"
alsoInTheDocument.change: A limit that is an analysis setting is written as a token, `{limit:<setting>}`, which the engine fills with the number and its unit ("over 200 KB", "more than 1 second"). A number that is a fixed rule of the check, or Google's, stays a number ("2 MB", "10 steps").

alsoInTheDocument.where: The rules, "A Notice always says when it is fine"
alsoInTheDocument.change: Six Notices have no honest "nothing to do" and say when it can wait: empty-anchor-text, h1-missing, h1-multiple, security-headers-missing, lang-missing, charset-missing.
